Rakshak SOS — tap to send emergency alert
A personal safety tool that texts your trusted contacts when you need help.
You start SOS with the button, the widget, the Quick Settings tile or Volume Guard. A 3-second countdown lets you cancel.
Rakshak sends an SMS with your location to your emergency contacts.
Messages are sent from your phone\'s SIM, so your carrier\'s SMS charges may apply.

Rakshak does not replace emergency services. If you are in danger, call 112 (or your local emergency number) first whenever you can. SMS can fail or be delayed if there is no signal, no SIM or no balance.
Your contacts stay on this phone. Rakshak has no account, no server, no analytics and no ads, and it cannot connect to the internet. Your location and messages are used only when you trigger SOS.

Volume Guard uses an accessibility service

To notice Volume Up and Volume Down pressed together, Rakshak needs its accessibility service turned on in Android Settings.

The service only watches those two keys. It does not read your screen, other apps, passwords or anything you type, and it sends no data anywhere.

When you press both keys, a 3-second countdown starts and you can cancel it. If you do not turn this on, you can still use the SOS button, the widget and the Quick Settings tile.

Your emergency contacts (name and phone number) are stored on this phone. They may be included in your Android / Google backup. Rakshak also keeps the status of your most recent SOS (which contacts were alerted) so it can finish after an interruption.

Alerts are sent from your SIM straight to your contacts. Rakshak has no server and cannot read your other messages.

The SOS button, the home screen widget, the Quick Settings tile and Volume Guard. Each one starts a 3-second countdown with Cancel and Send now. Android may ask you to unlock your phone before it runs a Quick Settings tile. Rakshak does not use the microphone.

Rakshak keeps a short list of your last 20 SOS events on this phone: the time, what started it, how many contacts were reached and whether location was shared. It holds no phone numbers and no coordinates, it is not included in backups, and you can clear it at any time. Test messages are never recorded.
